scope: Only the7 user-provided canonical originals; no experiments, remote execution or implementation. Identity checks are separate from mechanism and effectiveness judgments.
quote_rule: pdftotext per PDF file page; NFKC, remove end-of-line word hyphenation, collapse whitespace; quote must occur on the specified page. Formula/table readings require visual check and remain distinct from literal text checks.

papers.version: IEEE publisher PDF, 11 file pages = journal532–542
papers.mechanism: Cable-driven planar joystick force control. Actor/critic online RL; state contains mean/peak positive and negative directional errors. g is bounded impedance gain, not a psychological score. Actor cost Eq9 squares a Uc-weighted mixture of predicted error cost and g; Eq11 adjusts Uc using recent performance; Eq12 attempts curriculum adaptation through acceptable-error threshold eta. Fig3 explicitly links evaluation, RL and impedance control.
papers.reference_and_calibration: e_neg is a physical-engagement proxy under force perturbation, not independently measured active torque or psychological engagement. Mean g is a robot-assistance surrogate, not measured assistive work/exposure. PRE critic pre-training uses g=0. eta thresholds uniform/manual; learning rates pilot-derived.
papers.population_design: 15 healthy adults, 11 male,18–32; two within-subject visits at least48h apart, balanced controller order; RL-AAN vs ILC-AAN, four180-cycle training sessions. PT at1/10/20min, force perturbation without assistance. Catch-trial subset N=6.
papers.effects_and_nulls: TableII: training under-correction improves for both; no significant controller difference in this training reduction. RL-AAN g estimated controller contrast -0.04(0.008),p<.001; retention under-correction contrast28.3(6.4),p<.001. Training over-correction session trend and retention are different endpoints. Retention e_neg contrasts nonsignificant; do not call all endpoints improved. TableIV catch trials both p<.001, subset N=6.
papers.dose_psychology_safety: Performance-based assistance/difficulty adaptation, repetition counts and breaks are reported; not an identified patient dose-response or psychological construct measurement. Uniform parameters, no unguided visual-feedback control, no stroke efficacy conclusion. Consent and bounded controller parameters are not clinical safety validation.
papers.novelty_consequence: Eliminates broad novelty claims of RL+AAN, personalization, error/assistance dynamic tradeoff or joint assistance/difficulty adaptation. Does not resolve independent dual-construct references or error/OOD authorization.

visual_check.observation: Rendered originalPDF pages read, plots/tables readable. Original Eq12 prints max(eta_low,eta-zeta) for increasing challenge and min(eta_high,eta+zeta) for easing, but the text assigns eta_low=5mm and eta_high=2mm. This is a documented boundary-symbol ambiguity; do not silently repair or infer the authors' implementation. Curriculum prior still exists regardless of this replication ambiguity.

Article's integral-of-absolute-interaction-force label Eq18 is RMS-like aggregation, not robot assistive work or integrated energy/dose.

papers.reference_and_calibration: Static locked-robot labels are measured interaction force, taken as voluntary force under static assumption. papers.version: IEEE publisher PDF,9 file pages=journal1351–1359;Apr2021,first publication2020
papers.mechanism: End-effector position/error and velocity→3-region resistance/assistance/restriction→fuzzy-assisted stiffness adjustment(error+error-rate)→cable force/PID. Small-error region adds resistance/difficulty, intermediate assists, boundary overshoot uses restriction damping and stiffness decay. Fuzzy membership is not calibrated observation/effort probability.
papers.reference_and_calibration: Four measured cable tensions map toFc; human active force approximated as-Fc assuming small end-effector mass/acceleration. Author explicitly calls for a3D end-effector force sensor later. AAF, MAE and mode occupancy are physical/engineering performance, not independent biological active contribution or delivered-work truth.
papers.population_design: 10 healthy,6male/4female,mean25.3years; four perturbation levelsD0–D3, each4×30s circular XZ trajectories,10min rest between trials. Random artificial force disturbances simulate reduced performance, not actual stroke disability/patient recovery.
papers.effects_and_nulls: Friedman and Wilcoxon with Bonferroni p<.008; D0–D1 andD2–D3 lack corrected significance in MAE/AAF comparisons. Increasing disturbance increases error and assistance occupancy; restriction exposure near0. Demonstrates controller response, not training-benefit causation or clinical safety. AAF relates to cable-force approximation; not physical effort truth.
papers.dose_psychology_safety: Difficulty/assistance switching precedes this project; repetition duration/rest explicit but no clinical dose or psychological scale. Position boundary, tension limits and scram button are guards, not fault/OOD clinical safety validation. Clinical trials and better impairment simulation are future work.
papers.novelty_consequence: Blocks generic performance-driven assistance/resistance/difficulty or adding fuzzy uncertainty novelty. C3 must exceed an already existing restriction mode/hardware guard and conditional theory, not rename safeguards.
